en: Do you carry a fish?
explain: _-ne_ on the first word turns a statement into a yes/no question: _portāsne_. Nothing else changes.
distractors: Portās piscem?
Without _-ne_ this is still a statement. Add _-ne_ to the first word to ask: _portāsne_.
Portāsne pisce?
_pisce_ is ablative singular, but it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative: _piscem_.
Portābisne piscem?
_portābis_ is 2nd person singular (future tense) of _portō_ (“you will carry”), but here you need 2nd person singular (present tense): _portās_.

en: You do not carry a fish.
explain: _nōn_ means “not” and goes right before the verb: _nōn portās_.
distractors: Pisce nōn portās.
_pisce_ is ablative singular, but it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative: _piscem_.
Piscem portās nōn.
_nōn_ goes before the verb it negates: _nōn portās_.
Piscem nōn portō.
_portō_ is 1st person singular (present tense) of _portō_ (“I carry”), but here you need 2nd person singular (present tense): _portās_.
